script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. BUSY STREET - DAY

A crowd of people scurry down the sidewalk, passing by JEN, a 35-year-old woman, who leans against a lamppost, staring at her phone with a disheartened expression.

JEN
(whispering to herself)
One more rejection...

Suddenly, her phone beeps. She looks up, hopeful.

INT. JEN'S APARTMENT - LIVING ROOM - DAY

Jen sits at her kitchen table, surrounded by resumes and rejection letters, her face expressionless as she reads an email from an unknown sender.

JEN
(to herself)
Another casting call? Let me check.

INT. AUDITION ROOM - DAY

Jen enters a dimly lit room, filled with eager actors. She spots an older man, GORDON, sitting alone at a table, poring over a stack of resumes.

GORDON
(looks up, smiles)
Ah, Jen, welcome back. How was your commute?

JEN
(sighs)
Same old, Gordon.

INT. GORDON'S OFFICE - DAY

Gordon sits behind his desk, looking at Jen with concern.

GORDON
Jen, I've seen your talent. I've seen your dedication. But the reality is, the acting industry is tough. And sometimes, you need to explore other options to make a living.

JEN
(defensive)
I don't want to give up. I can do this.

GORDON
(leaning forward)
I believe in you. But what about a career in writing? You have a way with words.

INT. JEN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jen sits at her computer, typing furiously. She's writing her first screenplay.

INT. CAFETERIA - DAY

Jen meets with a group of writers, all of whom have successful careers. They offer her advice and encouragement.

WRITER 1
Just keep writing. The more you write, the better you'll get.

WRITER 2
And don't give up your day job just yet. You need to save money for the inevitable ups and downs.

WRITER 3
(laughs)
And good luck with the all-nighters. Trust me, we've all been there.

INT. JEN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jen's eyes are red and swollen from lack of sleep. She looks at the stack of papers covering her desk, her laptop open beside them.

JEN
(talking to herself)
I can do this. I have to do this.

INT. WRITING FESTIVAL - DAY

Jen attends a writing festival, where she pitches her screenplay to producers. She's nervous but determined.

INT. PRODUCER'S OFFICE - DAY

Jen sits across from a producer, who listens intently as she pitches her screenplay.

PRODUCER
(leaning back in his chair)
Interesting. I'll have my team read it and get back to you.

INT. JEN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jen waits anxiously by the phone, hoping for good news.

INT. PRODUCER'S OFFICE - DAY

The producer calls Jen with an offer to produce her screenplay.

PRODUCER
(over the phone)
Congratulations, Jen. We're going to make your screenplay into a movie.

INT. SET - DAY

Jen watches as her screenplay comes to life on the big screen. She's surrounded by a cast and crew that believe in her talent.

JEN
(whispering to herself)
I did it.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
